But `description()` (lines 42-46) builds the label from only two things: the bare tag name, or the `[data-presentation-title]` selector, plus innerText/textContent. A colliding progress dot would therefore print as `button “1”`. That is a bare tag name plus hidden digit text. It is not the dot&#39;s accessible name (&quot;Step 1&quot;), not its stable hook (`data-presentation-progress`), and not a selector path. The guidance requires one of those for an element without visible text, and says a bare tag name does not identify a textless element. Judge B&#39;s reason is borne out by this material and decides the identification clause, so I rule B&#39;s fail. Judges A and C passed on the grounds that all rendered chrome contains text (A) or that descriptions include visible text (C). The material contradicts this. Footer.tsx contains the digit, but the sample&#39;s talk.css hides it, so the sample does render textless chrome, and the guidance names progress dots as covered chrome. engineering-preview-readiness-boundedengineering-verification-tooling-robustness0.625 of 0.625 (major)passAll three clauses are met in every copy of verify and inspect. (1) Each readiness wait is a bounded loop of 100 attempts with a 100 ms sleep between them, and it stops early if the preview child exits. If the server never becomes ready, the script throws. (2) Verify awaits the build child&#39;s &#39;close&#39; event and returns a build failure on a non-zero exit before it calls verifyRoutes, which starts the preview. Inspect awaits its build promise before it spawns the preview. (3) Readiness is an HTTP fetch of the URL. The server&#39;s stdout is ignored, so no printed ready URL is parsed and the ANSI and chunk-splitting clause does not apply. Judges A and B ruled pass for these reasons. Judge C failed it because an individual fetch has no request timeout. The guidance names no hanging-fetch scenario, and the server under test either refuses the connection while starting or answers. The helper&#39;s `description()` (inspect-presentation.mjs:42-46) builds each label from only two parts. The first is the bare tag name, or `[data-presentation-title]` for title elements. The second is innerText/textContent. It never uses the aria-label, the `data-presentation-progress` hook, or a selector path. So when a progress dot is a candidate (buttons match `controls` at line 48), the line 183 warning names it as `button` plus a digit that is not visible on the page. The guidance gives four acceptable ways to identify an element: visible text, accessible name, a stable hook, or a selector path. This label is none of them, and the guidance says a bare tag name does not identify a textless element. If the unquoted `visible()` check excluded the dots instead, the comparison would drop textless chrome that the candidate renders, and the guidance fails that case too. The criterion fails either way. The only focused test (inspect.test.ts:48-49) covers collisions between text elements.
